# AI Chat Reporting — Vars

Var definitions are derived from `module.lowdefy.yaml`. Pass these via the `vars:` block in your app's `lowdefy.yaml` entry for this module.

## Summary

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `catalog` | object |  | Yes | The collections catalog — the data dictionary AND the confidentiality/authorization boundary. A map keyed by collection name (`{ [collectionName]: { roles, description, fields, relationships } }`); `collection` and every `$lookup.from` in an AI-authored pipeline must be a key of this map, and the engine enforces the union of the touched collections' `roles` (base plus all lookups, recursively). Declaring a collection here is the act of exposing it. Per-entry keys — `roles` (optional string[] of user roles allowed to query this collection; ABSENT or EMPTY means any authenticated user may query it — role-gating is opt-in), `description` (what the collection holds — prompt material for the agent), `fields` (optional map of field name → `{ type: one of string\|number\|boolean\|date\|object\|array, description, values (optional enum values — feeds report select-filter options), and the optional display hints format, currency, locale, decimals — prompt material the agent copies into presentation contracts, never enforcement }`), and `relationships` (optional array of `{ field, collection, foreignField }` declaring which fields join to which collections so the agent can author correct `$lookup`s). Feeds the agent's instructions at build time and is the allowlist every pipeline validates against. To expose a collection while hiding some fields (or to pre-bake array/object-array/cross- collection joins at a fixed grain), declare a read-only MongoDB view as a first-class catalog entry — see the "reporting over complex data" guide.  |
| `app_context` | string |  |  | Project context injected verbatim into the reporting agent's instructions, under an "About this application" heading between the agent's role and the pipeline-authoring rules. Use it for what the catalog cannot express: what the app is for, domain vocabulary and synonyms users will type, business rules the agent should assume (fiscal year, which statuses count as "open", how "active" is defined), and preferences for how to answer. Markdown is fine. Omitted from the prompt entirely when not set — the agent works without it, and it is never validation: nothing here widens what the agent may query, which remains exactly what `catalog` declares.  |
| `reports_collection` | string | `report_layouts` |  | Collection name for saved report specs. The default is `report_layouts` although this module and every endpoint call them reports — the name is left over from an earlier concept and is deliberately NOT renamed: changing the default would silently point an existing app at an empty collection.  |
| `share_roles` | array |  |  | User roles whose holders may publish a saved report to the whole app. A string array — more than one role can legitimately carry the privilege. Checked server-side by set-report-visibility, never in the UI: a hidden menu item is an affordance, the match in the endpoint is the authorization. Publishing and unpublishing are gated differently, deliberately. Publishing requires the caller to be the report's owner AND to hold one of these roles. Unpublishing requires the caller to be the owner OR to hold one of them — so a share_roles holder can retract a report they do not own (anyone trusted to decide what the whole app sees is trusted to decide it should stop seeing something), and a report stays retractable after its author's role is revoked, after the author leaves, or after this var is removed. There is no equivalent power to publish, rename, delete or edit someone else's report. Unset means nothing can be published: every publish call is rejected and no publish control renders anywhere. It is NOT a retroactive switch — reports already shared stay listed and readable, and their owners can still unpublish them.  |
| `conversations_collection` | string | `conversations` |  | Collection name for chat conversations. |
| `model` | string | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` |  | Gateway model id (provider/model) for the reporting assistant, e.g. anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 or anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5.  |
| `welcome` | object |  |  | Copy for the chat page's empty state — the surface that teaches both of the module's jobs, asking a question and building a report. Six leaves: a title, a line naming what the assistant can see, and a label plus a starter-prompt list per job track. This copy feeds the AgentChat block's `welcome` property, which the chat page maps to a two-track shape: the block renders the tracks in-flow as the transcript's leading item, so the empty state scrolls up with the conversation and stays reachable by scrolling back rather than being hidden on the first send.  |

## Nested var details

### `welcome`

Copy for the chat page's empty state — the surface that teaches both of the module's jobs, asking a question and building a report. Six leaves: a title, a line naming what the assistant can see, and a label plus a starter-prompt list per job track. This copy feeds the AgentChat block's `welcome` property, which the chat page maps to a two-track shape: the block renders the tracks in-flow as the transcript's leading item, so the empty state scrolls up with the conversation and stays reachable by scrolling back rather than being hidden on the first send.

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | `Ask about your data` |  | The heading shown above both starter tracks. |
| `data_scope` | string |  |  | One line naming what the assistant can see, in the words this app's users use — e.g. "I can see your orders, customers and shipments." NO default: there is no generic sentence true of every app, and a wrong one is a promise the agent then fails to keep, so when unset the line is simply not rendered — it never falls back to collection names. Deliberately not derived from `catalog`: a collection is not an entity a user recognises (one collection can span several entities a user asks about by name, several collections can be one entity to a user, and a collection can be internal plumbing that should never appear in a welcome), and `catalog`'s per-collection `description` is prompt material for the agent, not copy written for a person.  |
| `explore_label` | string | `Get an answer` |  | Heading over the "ask a question" track's starters. An app whose users would not describe the module's other job as building a "report" should override this alongside `report_label`.  |
| `explore_starters` | array | _(see manifest)_ |  | Starter prompts for the "ask a question" track — a string array. Clicking a starter fills the composer rather than sending it, which is what makes a generic shipped default safe: a near-miss is an editable first draft, not a message the user never meant to send.  |
| `report_label` | string | `Build a report` |  | Heading over the "build a report" track's starters. An app whose users do not call the output a "report" should override this alongside `explore_label`.  |
| `report_starters` | array | _(see manifest)_ |  | Starter prompts for the "build a report" track — a string array. Clicking a starter fills the composer rather than sending it, which is what makes a generic shipped default safe: a near-miss is an editable first draft, not a message the user never meant to send.  |
